brief.job: Move available agents to the queue most likely to breach its response commitment.
brief.consequence: Misallocation breaches contracted response times and leaves customers waiting without a credible answer.
facts: The lead is responsible for Billing, Login, API, and General queues during the next hour.
Billing has 38 open conversations, 7 agents, a median first response of 18 minutes against a 30-minute target, and 3 conversations due within 10 minutes.
Login has 16 open conversations, 3 agents, a median first response of 22 minutes against a 20-minute target, and 5 conversations due within 10 minutes.
API has 24 open conversations, 4 agents, a median first response of 44 minutes against a 60-minute target, and 1 conversation due within 10 minutes.
General has 71 open conversations, 9 agents, a median first response of 95 minutes against a 120-minute target, and no conversation due within 10 minutes.
Two agents are available to reassign. Reassignment is reversible. Escalating an individual conversation pages the specialist and should not be the default queue action.
The current hour has 38% more Login arrivals than the previous hour; the other queues are within 10% of their prior-hour arrival counts.

required_interactions: Reassign an available agent to a queue
Inspect the conversations closest to breach
acceptance_checks: The queue at greatest near-term risk is visually and verbally distinguishable from high-volume but lower-risk queues.
The action hierarchy keeps escalation secondary to allocation.
The surface preserves the stated queue facts without invented agent performance data.
